subject.title: [Feature]: Subagent session reuse for expert agents (avoid new session per spawn)

question: Should native `sessions_spawn` gain an opt-in core reuse/pooling API, should Teams gain channel session binding first, or should native subagent runs remain isolated with reuse limited to ACP and thread-bound sessions?
rationale: The missing source path is clear, but the permanent answer changes session-state semantics, model-facing tool/API surface, concurrency behavior, cleanup, and channel ownership boundaries.

options.title: Design core opt-in native reuse
options.body: Add an explicit scoped native reuse contract only after deciding TTL/liveness, locking, cleanup, and history-isolation rules.

options.title: Add Teams binding first
options.body: Implement Teams through the channel conversation/session-binding seam and keep ordinary native `mode="run"` isolated.

options.title: Keep native runs isolated
options.body: Document ACP resume and thread-bound sessions as the supported reuse paths and close native run reuse as out of scope.

recommendation.title: Design core opt-in native reuse
recommendation.body: Add an explicit scoped native reuse contract only after deciding TTL/liveness, locking, cleanup, and history-isolation rules.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest current history across the native spawn path, Teams plugin boundary, and session-state review surface.
